newsitem.title: GERMANY: German debt and futures modestly up in late trade.
newsitem.headline: German debt and futures modestly up in late trade.

text.p: German Bunds and futures were modestly higher in late dealings on Thursday, recovering slightly after December M3 money supply data was stronger than expected and the Bundesbank kept rates steady at a meeting.
DTB March Bund futures were up five basis points at 101.59 in late dealings but off the session high at 101.76.

Traders said the market was consolidating while waiting for fresh fundamentals, including Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's testimony to Congress next Tuesday, with no major German economic data expected to be released on Friday.
Market attention focused on the release of December M3, which showed growth slowing marginally to an annualised rate of 7.9 percent from November's 8.0 percent.

But it was above market forecasts for a rate of 7.6 percent and dealers said the news dampened hopes for a credit easing anytime soon. The Bundesbank later on Thursday announced that it had kept rates steady after a council meeting.
But Bunds showed their usual disdain for domestic news as investors continued to focus on more international issues than on proposed changes to Germany's tax structure.
Market attention on Friday will be on the U.S. market and also technical factors will be at the forefront, with March Bund resistance at 101.88 and 102.07 and support at 101.20.
